title: Australia Post's reserved letter service
summary: Australia Post has the exclusive right to carry letters within Australia under section 29 of the Australian Postal Corporation Act 1989, with exceptions that include letters over 250 grams. Letters are a shrinking market, but no rival may compete to deliver ordinary letters.
direction_rationale: A statutory monopoly bars rivals from carrying ordinary letters; it funds Australia Post's universal service obligation, which is not weighed here.

verified.notes: An existing setting: no commencement date is recorded. Act identifier from the Federal Register of Legislation; the 250 gram threshold is from the department's Australia Post page.
